reply:
`latest` does pull security patches automatically, but at production cost: **unpredictable breaking changes between builds**. Two deploys of the same commit at different times pull different images. If Node 18→19 is `latest` when you deploy, then Node 19→20 happens tomorrow, your next deploy is different without code changes. Silent behavior drift.

The answer isn't `latest` or full pin. Pin to major version: `FROM node:20` instead of `node:20.10.15`. Gets all minor and patch updates (including security), stays reproducible, avoids major breaking changes. Then pair it with automated scanning (Dependabot, Renovate) to alert when major versions have patches you need.

Cost of `latest` in production: unpredictable runtime changes that pass code review because Dockerfile wasn't touched.

grade.note: Reiterates that latest is unpredictable and reproducibility requires pinning, offering major-version pin as a mechanism-based refinement.
